questions.question: Which prized deep-red semi-precious stone was obtained from Gujarat and processed into beads at Harappan workshop centers?
questions.explanation: Carnelian was procured from Bharuch and Saurashtra; Harappan artisans baked it to acquire its rich red colour before drilling.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya established the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE after overthrowing which last ruler of the Nanda dynasty?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya, ousted Dhana Nanda, the last monarch of the powerful Nanda dynasty of Magadha.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Which Gupta emperor defeated the Western Kshatrapas and adopted the legendary imperial title 'Vikramaditya'?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II extended Gupta power to the western seaboard and assumed the title of Vikramaditya.

questions.question: According to Indian literary tradition, who was the revered sage who composed the original Sanskrit epic Ramayana?
questions.explanation: Sage Valmiki is recognized as the Adi Kavi who composed the Sanskrit epic Ramayana.

questions.question: In Buddhist spiritual philosophy, what is the literal meaning of the ultimate goal 'Nirvana'?
options: A) The extinguishing or blowing out of the flame of ego and desire
B) Ascending to a celestial golden paradise
C) Merging into the cosmic world soul Brahman
D) Rebirth as an immortal king on earth
questions.explanation: Nirvana literally means blowing out or extinguishing the flame of human craving and sorrow, ending the cycle of rebirth.

questions.question: The Moroccan scholar Ibn Battuta served as the imperial Qazi (judge) of Delhi under Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq for approximately how many years?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta served as the Qazi of Delhi for about eight years until a temporary estrangement with the Sultan.

questions.question: Which female Shaivite Bhakti saint of Tamil Nadu renounced her physical beauty to adopt an emaciated ascetic form, composing passionate verses to Shiva?
questions.explanation: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was an ardent Shaiva devotee who discarded youthful beauty to become an ascetic singer at cremation grounds.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The magnificent ruined capital of the Vijayanagara Empire situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra is recognized globally today as:
questions.explanation: The ruins of the Vijayanagara imperial capital at Hampi were declared a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: The imperial policy of universal peace and religious coexistence formulated by Akbar and articulated by Abu'l Fazl was known as:
questions.explanation: Sulh-i Kul meant absolute universal peace, where all religions were tolerated provided they did not undermine state stability.

questions.question: Which East India Company surgeon and surveyor prepared exhaustive statistical surveys and natural history journals of eastern India between 1807 and 1814?
questions.explanation: Francis Buchanan toured the territories of Bengal and Bihar, compiling surveys on geology, agriculture, and social customs.

questions.question: In 1855, which British Resident of Lucknow submitted a damning report asserting that Awadh suffered from extreme maladministration, laying the pretext for annexation?
questions.explanation: Outram's official report depicted Awadh as hopelessly misgoverned, which Lord Dalhousie cited to annex the territory in 1856.

questions.question: In 1918, Mahatma Gandhi undertook a hunger strike in support of industrial workers demanding a wage hike in which city?
questions.explanation: In 1918, Gandhi intervened in the Ahmedabad mill strike, undertaking a fast to secure a 35% wage increase for textile workers.

questions.question: Which Harappan city situated on Kadir Island in the Rann of Kachchh is architecturally unique for its tripartite division into Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town?
questions.explanation: Unlike most Harappan sites divided into two parts, Dholavira features three distinct fortified sectors built of dressed stone.

questions.question: What functional use did Harappan inhabitants make of triangular baked terracotta cakes found in large numbers near hearths and pottery kilns?
options: A) Standard currency tokens for purchasing imported dried fish
B) Retaining and radiating uniform thermal heat inside ovens, hearths, and kilns
C) Weights for sinking marine fishing nets in tidal estuaries
D) Votive amulets offered to fertility mother goddesses
questions.explanation: Terracotta cakes were heat retainers placed in domestic ovens and kilns to maintain steady ceramic firing temperatures.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In ancient northern India, the historic highway that connected Pataliputra through Mathura and Taxila to Central Asian trans-continental trade routes was known as:
questions.explanation: The Uttarapatha was the vital overland commercial route connecting the Gangetic plains to northwestern frontier passes.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Which south Indian royal dynasty is celebrated for creating the monolithic rock-cut Five Rathas at the coastal port city of Mahabalipuram?
questions.explanation: The Pallava rulers, particularly Narasimhavarman I Mamalla, excavated the monolithic granite rathas at Mahabalipuram.

questions.question: In early Sanskrit literature and Brahmanical law books, what did the term 'Mlechchha' designate?
options: A) Foreigners or communities residing outside the Sanskrit linguistic and Aryan cultural sphere
B) Court royal priests who performed daily fire sacrifices
C) High-ranking commanders of the royal elephant corps
D) Wandering Buddhist monks practicing celibacy
questions.explanation: Sanskrit texts used Mlechchha to describe outsiders who spoke non-Indo-Aryan tongues and did not conform to varna norms.

questions.question: In the Mahabharata, the heroic archer Ekalavya who offered his severed thumb to Dronacharya belonged to which forest-dwelling community?
questions.explanation: Ekalavya was a prince of the Nishadas, an indigenous forest-dwelling tribal community outside the fourfold varna framework.

questions.question: In the architectural elements of an ancient Buddhist stupa, the umbrella structure rising from the harmika representing royal honor and protection is known as:
questions.explanation: The central mast (yashti) rising from the harmika was surmounted by symbolic royal umbrellas called chhatras.

questions.question: The legendary Jataka tales, which narrate didactic fables concerning the former lives of Gautama Buddha, were compiled in which language?
questions.explanation: The 547 Jataka tales were included in the Khuddaka Nikaya of the Pali Sutta Pitaka.

questions.question: Al-Biruni observed that individuals relegated below the four varnas who performed menial sanitation and disposal work were designated as:
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni noted eight classes of people called Antyaja who lived outside villages and performed hereditary leather, weaving, and scavenging crafts.

questions.question: Why did Francois Bernier maintain that the lack of private property in land under the Mughals was disastrous for the Indian economy?
options: A) Because European merchant fleets refused to buy grain from state-owned farms
B) Because crown ownership prevented landowners from passing property to descendants, discouraging long-term capital investment in agricultural improvement
C) Because peasant farmers were forbidden from digging freshwater irrigation canals
D) Because all harvested wheat was confiscated and dumped into the Yamuna river
questions.explanation: Bernier argued that crown land ownership led to agricultural ruin, contrasted with European private ownership that spurred improvements.

questions.question: Which prominent Chishti Sufi saint, succeeding Nizamuddin Auliya in the 14th century, was revered in Delhi as 'Chirag-i Dilli' (The Lamp of Delhi)?
questions.explanation: Shaikh Nasiruddin Mahmud was bestowed the title Chirag-i Dilli for his spiritual leadership in Delhi after Nizamuddin Auliya.

questions.question: Devotional verses of which non-Sikh Bhakti and Sufi mystics were included in the Sikh holy scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib?
options: A) Tulsidas, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, and Shankaradeva
B) Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, and Akkamahadevi
D) Baba Farid, Kabir, Bhagat Namdev, and Ravidas
questions.explanation: The Guru Granth Sahib includes compositions of 15 non-Sikh bhagats, including Baba Farid, Kabir, Namdev, and Ravidas.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Which Portuguese visitor to Vijayanagara in 1520 was impressed by the city's vast size, writing that it was as large as Rome and replete with luxury goods?
questions.explanation: Domingo Paes left an admiring narrative of the bustling markets, royal palaces, and military reviews of Vijayanagara under Krishnadeva Raya.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Which stone aqueduct and canal constructed under the Sangama rulers drew water from a dam on the Tungabhadra to irrigate the valley between the Sacred and Urban Centres?
questions.explanation: The Hiriya canal carried water from a dam across the Tungabhadra to irrigate the fertile agricultural valley within the city walls.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the land revenue classification of the Ain-i-Akbari, how was 'Parauti' land defined?
options: A) Land that had been abandoned for half a century due to chronic war
B) Land irrigated exclusively by imperial Persian wheels
C) Land that was left uncultivated temporarily for a year or two to allow the soil to naturally recover its nutrients
D) Land gifted tax-free to Sufi hospices
questions.explanation: Parauti was land left out of cultivation for a short interval so that it could recover its natural strength.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the cyclical agrarian rhythm of Mughal India, what was the 'Kharif' cropping season?
options: A) The spring crop sown in winter and harvested in March-April
B) The dry summer crop cultivated exclusively along river sandbanks
C) The perennial fruit crop harvested throughout the year
D) The autumn crop sown at the onset of the summer monsoon and harvested in autumn
questions.explanation: Kharif crops (such as rice, maize, and cotton) were monsoon crops, while Rabi crops (wheat, gram, barley) were winter crops.

questions.question: The British colonial government formally carved out and demarcated the forest tract of 'Damin-i-Koh' in 1832 for which purpose?
options: A) To settle the immigrant Santhals in a designated territory to encourage settled plough agriculture
B) To establish an artillery testing ground for the Bengal Native Infantry
C) To build a network of tea plantations managed by British joint-stock companies
D) To create a wildlife sanctuary protecting elephants
questions.explanation: Damin-i-Koh ('skirts of the hills') was demarcated with boundary pillars in 1832 to settle Santhals as cultivators.

questions.question: Under the Ryotwari settlement introduced in the Bombay and Madras Presidencies, with whom did the British administration settle land revenue?
options: A) With hereditary aristocratic zamindars possessing private armies
B) Directly with the individual peasant cultivator (the ryot)
C) With the corporate village community represented by village headmen
D) With chartered European commercial shipping companies
questions.explanation: In the Ryotwari system, the state contracted directly with the ryot (cultivator), assessing land revenue based on periodic soil surveys.

questions.question: Which charismatic preacher and rebel leader in Faizabad moved from village to village preaching jihad against British rule, defeating British forces at the Battle of Chinhat?
questions.explanation: Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah traveled with drums and palanquins, preaching rebellion against the British, and played a prominent military role in Awadh.

questions.question: The greased paper cartridges of the new Enfield rifle introduced in early 1857 were rumored among sepoys to be lubricated with fat from which animals?
questions.explanation: The cartridges had to be bitten off before loading; rumors that they were greased with cow fat (sacred to Hindus) and pig fat (forbidden to Muslims) ignited rebellion.

questions.question: Vallabhbhai Patel was conferred the affectionate title 'Sardar' by local peasant women following the triumph of which non-violent satyagraha campaign in 1928?
questions.explanation: Patel's leadership of the Bardoli peasant campaign against an exorbitant 22% land tax increase earned him the title of Sardar.

questions.question: What was the principal outcome agreed upon between Viceroy Lord Irwin and Mahatma Gandhi in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931?
options: A) The British government granted immediate Dominion Status to India
B) The Congress agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and participate in the Second Round Table Conference
C) The salt tax was permanently removed from all colonial statutes
D) All political prisoners accused of violent revolutionary assassinations were released
questions.explanation: The pact led to the suspension of Civil Disobedience, release of non-violent prisoners, and Gandhi's journey to London for talks.

questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly of India, who served as the Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, and Tribal Areas?
questions.explanation: Sardar Patel presided over this crucial committee, steering the formulation of fundamental rights and safeguards for minorities.

questions.question: At Harappa's Cemetery R-37, archaeological excavation revealed which rare mortuary practice among certain elite interments?
options: A) Cremation on raised basalt pyres followed by immersion of ashes in bronze urns
B) Mummification using natron salts and wrapping in Persian silk bandages
C) Exposure on tall stone towers to birds of prey followed by mass ossuary burial
D) Burial within a hollowed-out wooden coffin constructed of rosewood with a deodar lid inside a mud-brick pit
questions.explanation: Mortimer Wheeler and subsequent excavators found wooden coffins made of local rosewood and cedar lids in Cemetery R-37 at Harappa.

questions.question: How did Harappan artisans manufacture the lustrous, glass-like composite material known as 'Faience'?
options: A) By grinding silica sand or crushed quartz, mixing it with gum and mineral colourants, and then firing it at high temperature to produce a vitreous glaze
B) By carving solid jade boulders imported directly from Central Asian riverbeds
C) By casting molten tin into stone moulds lined with animal tallow
D) By dipping dried terracotta figurines into liquid cinnabar and mercury
questions.explanation: Faience was an artificial material produced by grinding quartz sand, mixing with binder, shaping, and firing to produce a glassy finish.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In early historical India, merchant and craft guilds (Shrenis) maintained considerable institutional autonomy by possessing:
options: A) Veto power over the appointment of crown princes in imperial dynasties
B) Their own customary laws, independent judicial assemblies, private armed militias (Shreni-bala), and minting corporate coinage
C) Monopoly rights over ocean piracy along the Arabian sea coastline
D) Exclusive privileges to conduct Vedic Rajasuya sacrifices on behalf of monarchs
questions.explanation: Shrenis had corporate autonomy: they formulated their own guild rules, maintained private armed forces (shreni-bala), and issued urban coins.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: The famous monolithic stone pillar at Besnagar (Vidisha) was dedicated to Lord Vasudeva by Heliodorus, who was an ambassador dispatched by which Indo-Greek king?
questions.explanation: The Besnagar pillar inscription records that Heliodorus, an envoy of King Antialcidas of Taxila, erected the Garuda pillar as a Bhagavata devotee.

questions.question: In ancient Hindu jurisprudence, how did the Dayabhaga legal system of Bengal differ from the widespread Mitakshara legal system?
options: A) Under Dayabhaga, all ancestral land was surrendered to the local Buddhist sangha upon the father's death
B) Under Dayabhaga, daughters received double the share of ancestral estates compared to eldest sons
C) Under Dayabhaga, property was owned collectively by the entire village without private title
D) Under Dayabhaga, sons acquired no right in ancestral property by mere birth during their father's life, and a childless widow could inherit her husband's share
questions.explanation: In Mitakshara, sons acquire birthrights in coparcenary property; in Dayabhaga (formulated by Jimutavahana), property passes only upon the father's death.

questions.question: At the Great Stupa of Sanchi, which narrative sculptural panel carved on the Northern Gateway illustrates the ultimate perfection of generosity (Dana)?
options: A) The Vessantara Jataka, depicting the prince who gave away his royal white elephant, his chariot, and his children
B) The Mahakapi Jataka, depicting the monkey king who stretched his body across the Ganga to rescue his troop
C) The Chhaddanta Jataka, depicting the six-tusked elephant offering his ivory tusks to a hunter
D) The Ruru Jataka, depicting the golden deer rescuing a drowning nobleman
questions.explanation: The Northern Gateway at Sanchi depicts Prince Vessantara giving away all his possessions in boundless compassion and generosity.

questions.question: In his travelogue, Ibn Battuta described an extraordinary commercial marketplace in Daulatabad dedicated exclusively to music, musicians, and female courtesan-singers known as:
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta marvelled at Tarababad in Daulatabad, a marketplace crowded with shops of male and female singers, decorated with swings.

questions.question: The foundational devotional anthology of the Tamil Shaivite Nayanars containing the sacred hymns of Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar is known as:
questions.explanation: The Tevaram constitutes the first seven books of the Tirumurai, comprising the hymns of the three celebrated Nayanars Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: During the monumental Mahanavami festival at Vijayanagara, what crucial imperial ritual occurred on the tenth and culminating day?
options: A) The royal court embarked on an oceanic pilgrimage to the island of Ceylon
B) The royal palace doors were thrown open for three days of public gambling
C) All stone temples throughout the empire were whitewashed with lime made from seashells
D) The monarch inspected his grand armed forces, war elephants, and cavalry in a vast open parade field, receiving tributes and presenting robes of honour to nayakas
questions.explanation: On the tenth day of Navaratri (Dussehra), the king reviewed his troops and accepted formal homage and gifts from subordinate nayakas.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Under the Mughal 'Zabt' land revenue assessment system, how was the state revenue demand calculated?
options: A) Through systematic land measurement and fixing the tax demand directly in cash using scheduled price-yield tables per bigha (Dastur)
B) By visually guessing the standing crop yield on horseback without measurement (Kankut)
C) By dividing the harvested grain heaps on the threshing floor into three heaps (Batai)
D) By levying a flat poll tax on every male villager regardless of land ownership
questions.explanation: Zabt was based on physical land survey (measurement) and schedule of cash rates (dastur-al-amal) for each crop per unit area.

questions.question: Francis Buchanan's account of Dinajpur district revealed that affluent jotedars frequently leased out tracts of land to sharecroppers who surrendered half the produce, known locally as:
questions.explanation: Buchanan documented that jotedars did not cultivate their vast lands themselves, but leased them to adhiyars (sharecroppers) who gave half the crop.

questions.question: In the Meerut division during the revolt of 1857, which rebel leader organized the Jat peasants across eighty-four villages (chaurasee des) of Baraut against British tax collectors?
questions.explanation: Shah Mal mobilized villagers of Baraut, cutting telegraph wires, supplying provisions to rebel Delhi, until he fell in battle in July 1857.

questions.question: The historic 'Independence Day' pledge taken across India on 26 January 1930 solemnly declared that:
options: A) India would join the British Commonwealth as an equal Dominion under the British Crown
B) The Congress would immediately launch armed attacks against colonial garrisons
C) Provincial autonomy under British governors would be accepted as an interim settlement
D) British rule had ruined India economically, politically, culturally, and spiritually, and it was a crime against man and God to submit to it any longer
questions.explanation: The 26 January 1930 pledge declared that freedom was an inalienable right, and submission to exploitative British rule was a crime against man and God.

questions.question: In the opening debates of the Constituent Assembly in December 1946, which Communist member from Bengal challenged the Assembly's autonomy, asserting it was functioning under the shadow of British guns?
questions.explanation: Somnath Lahiri argued that the Constituent Assembly was a British creation working under the limitations of the Cabinet Mission Plan.

questions.question: During the protracted debates on the official language in the Constituent Assembly, who formulated the historic compromise formula that designated Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language with English retained for fifteen years?
options: A) R.V. Dhulekar and Purushottam Das Tandon
B) Jawaharlal Nehru and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
C) Maulana Azad and Frank Anthony
D) K.M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
questions.explanation: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula resolved the bitter linguistic impasse by deciding that Hindi would be the 'official' language, with English continuing for 15 years.
